Cc: support@redwood.com
Date: 2028-07-20T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: High 5xx and timeouts calling Aether-3b starting 07/19

Hi Jonas,

We started seeing a spike in 5xx responses and timeouts from Aether-3b overnight (roughly 2028-07-19 23:40 UTC onward). Error rate jumped from ~0.4% to 8-12% on production traffic for our account (Prod namespace). Sample request IDs I grabbed from our gateway: req_84f2, req_84f8, req_8531 — all returned 503 or hung >30s.

This is impacting inference-heavy flows in our product; latency-sensitive customers are seeing errors. I attached a small log bundle (aether3b-client-logs.tar.gz) with request ids and timestamps. Can you confirm if there was a platform change or known degradation?

Thanks — we’re on an active release cycle so quick visibility would help.

— Elena
Director of ML Engineering
Novatech AI

Attachments: aether3b-client-logs.tar.gz
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>

Date: 2028-07-20T09:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: High 5xx and timeouts calling Aether-3b starting 07/19

Thanks for the report, Elena — sorry for the disruption. We’ve started triage. Initial notes:
- SRE (Markus) is looking at the serving fleet and kernel selection logs for the Aether-3b family.
- We’ve seen elevated GPU OOM retries and a small percentage of model-worker restarts in the Aether-3b pool between 23:30–02:20 UTC.
- As an immediate mitigation we’re enabling aggressive fallback routing for your account to Aether-3b-v2 (compatible weights, lower memory profile). That should reduce 5xx exposure within 10–15 minutes.

Could you confirm whether your requests require specific model variants or pinned versions? Also please send any recent config changes on your side (batching, max_seq_len) — that helps rule out client-side causes.

I’ve attached a request for logs (we’ll pull platform logs and share a metrics snapshot). I’ll keep you posted; Marissa will coordinate any credits / commercial follow-up.

— Jonas
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Date: 2028-07-21T08:15:00-07:00
Subject: FW: Aether-3b incident — postmortem draft for review

Team —

I drafted a short postmortem and remediation plan summarizing the root cause, impact, and action items. Key points:
- Root cause: a kernel selection optimization that was promoted to canary pools inadvertently increased memory churn for Aether-3b with mixed short/long sequences, causing worker evictions and a spike in transient 5xx responses.
- Impact: Novatech AI saw ~10% 5xx rate for ~3.5 hours (23:40–03:10 UTC); global fleet-wide effect was limited to 0.6% of total Aether-3b traffic.
- Remediation: rollback the kernel selection for affected pools, add a model-level memory-safety gate in compilation, expand canary sampling, and add a health-check threshold that prevents immediate promotion if eviction rate >0.1%.

Please review the attached draft (postmortem-draft-jonas.docx) and reply with comments. Marissa — I’ll need your final customer-facing summary and credit recommendation; Neha — please coordinate any commercial asks with Rajiv (Finosys) on the contract side.

Thanks,
Jonas

Subject: Aether-3b incident: final customer summary & next steps

Hi Elena — thanks again for your patience while we investigated. Below is a concise summary we’d like to share with your team. If you prefer a meeting, we can schedule one.

Summary of what happened
- Timeline: 2028-07-19T23:40 UTC through 2028-07-20T03:10 UTC (full recovery by 03:15 UTC).
- Root cause: a recently promoted kernel selection optimization increased memory pressure for the Aether-3b base binary when serving mixed short/long sequences, which led to frequent worker evictions and transient 5xx/timeouts.
- Scope: Novatech AI experienced ~10% elevated 5xxs for ~3.5 hours. The broader Aether-3b fleet impact was limited and mitigated quickly via rollbacks and routing.

What we did- Immediate: applied account-level fallback routing to Aether-3b-v2 for Novatech AI (10:50 PDT) which reduced exposure within minutes.
- Mitigation: paused the problematic kernel selection on affected pools and rolled a targeted patch to prevent aggressive memory allocation.
- Longer term: added a memory-safety gate in the compilation step, increased canary sample sizes, and implemented an eviction-rate health check to block promotions that cause >0.1% evictions.

What we’ll do for Novatech- Technical: provide the full platform logs and a sanitized metrics snapshot (attached).
- Commercial: we will apply a small service credit for the impacted calls under DEAL-4893; Neha will reach out to confirm credit amount and paperwork.
- Follow-up: we’ll share the finalized postmortem doc in Drive and offer a review call if helpful.

Attachments: aether3b-logs-20280719.zip, aether3b-metrics-snapshot-0720.json, postmortem-draft-jonas.docx

If you’d like more detail on the kernel change itself I can loop Markus in for a short technical session.

Best regards,
Marissa Cole
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference
